page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.1-4 is an entry-level virtual machine configuration within the flexible Standard3 compute series. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8358 processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.6 GHz. The allocation provides 1 dedicated physical core presenting 2 virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading, alongside 4.0 GB of system memory. This establishes a 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, offering focused core capacity for tasks with moderate memory requirements.

Hardware capabilities do not include local storage or discrete graphics processing units. Storage requirements must be satisfied through network-attached block volumes, while workloads requiring parallel compute must consider GPU-equipped alternatives. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The provision of dedicated rather than shared or burstable CPU cores eliminates cross-tenant interference and delivers consistent compute performance for small runtime envelopes without unneeded memory overhead.

The operational profile of VM.Standard3.Flex.1-4 makes it suitable for low-intensity computational jobs, lightweight microservices, and continuous integration workers. It functions reliably for dev-test pipelines, background cron utilities, API gateways, and light web serving tasks that operate within a compact 4.0 GB memory footprint.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.1-4 is an entry-tier x86_64 compute instance from the flexible Standard3 family, driven by an Intel Xeon 8358 processor running at 2.6 GHz. The configuration provisions 1 physical core with 2 vCPUs via hyperthreading, paired with 4.0 GB of memory to establish a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory profile. The instance features dedicated CPU allocation, avoiding resource contention from neighboring virtual machines, though it includes no onboard local storage or GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block volumes for system and application storage. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided. With its compact resource footprint and dedicated processor execution, VM.Standard3.Flex.1-4 serves as a cost-effective virtual hardware baseline for lightweight computational tasks. It fits microservices, development and testing environments, low-traffic web applications, utility automation, and small background workers that do not require high memory density or dense local disk arrays.
